ChainSwing.description: A double-pendulum swing built from pin joints and rigid links. Two chain segments hang from an anchor beam, ending in a glowing seat that receives periodic sinusoidal force. The trail draws the seat's arc through space, revealing how constraints propagate force through a chain — each link amplifying or dampening the one above. Arrow keys let you push the swing manually, hunting for resonance where small inputs produce large arcs.
ChainSwing.name: ChainSwing
ChainSwing.qfep_connection: Classical F — force as law transmitted through constraint chains. Each pin joint is a rule that permits rotation but forbids translation, and the emergent swing pattern is the system's negotiation between gravity and those rules.
ChainSwing.gamwell_reference: Mechanics of constrained motion, Lagrangian dynamics, coupled oscillators, double pendulum chaos
interactions: watch the periodic drive swing the seat automatically
press arrow keys to push the seat left or right
observe the trail drawing the seat's motion history
notice how joint markers glow at constraint points
ChainSwing.capacity: PREDICT how force propagates through a chain of pin joints by observing the relationship between driving frequency and swing amplitude.

CharacterRagdoll.description: A minimal ragdoll — one torso and one leg connected by a cone-twist joint at the hip. The joint limits swing to 35 degrees and twist to 25 degrees, mimicking the biomechanical range of a human hip. Press space to impulse the leg and watch how the cone-twist constraint channels the force into naturalistic swinging. This is the seed of character physics: from this single hip joint, the full ragdoll grows by adding more limbs and joints.
CharacterRagdoll.name: CharacterRagdoll
CharacterRagdoll.qfep_connection: Classical F moving toward phi — the cone-twist constraint at the hip is Form, but the emergent ragdoll motion hints at Entity. A body built from constraints begins to look like it has intention, even though it's purely mechanical.
CharacterRagdoll.gamwell_reference: Ragdoll physics, biomechanical joint modeling, character simulation, constrained multi-body dynamics, hip joint kinematics
interactions: press space to impulse the leg and watch hip-joint dynamics
observe how cone-twist limits produce naturalistic swing range
compare with ConeTwistBag for the same joint type on different geometry
CharacterRagdoll.capacity: BUILD a minimal ragdoll from rigid bodies and cone-twist joints and explain how joint limits produce biomechanically plausible motion.

ConeTwistBag.description: A punching bag hanging from a fixed anchor via a cone-twist joint. The cone-twist constraint limits the bag's swing to a 45-degree cone while allowing only 15 degrees of twist — like a ball-and-socket joint with angular limits. Nudge the bag and watch it swing within its invisible cone boundary, then slowly settle as damping absorbs the energy. The joint's bias and softness parameters control how sharply the limits are enforced.
ConeTwistBag.name: ConeTwistBag
ConeTwistBag.qfep_connection: Classical F — the cone-twist joint as an angular constraint that defines a region of permitted motion. The swing span and twist span are the Form parameters; the emergent pendular motion within that cone is the system's behavior.
ConeTwistBag.gamwell_reference: Ball-and-socket joints, angular constraints, cone-twist mechanics, biomechanical joint limits, pendular dynamics
interactions: press space to apply an impulse and watch the bag swing
observe the bag staying within its invisible cone boundary
notice how twist is more restricted than swing
ConeTwistBag.capacity: DISTINGUISH between swing span and twist span in a cone-twist joint and predict how angular limits shape pendular motion.

DrawbridgeHinge.description: A motorized drawbridge attached to a stone tower via a hinge joint. The motor rotates the bridge up and down within an 85-degree arc. Arrow keys control the motor velocity; when idle, the bridge gently oscillates with a sinusoidal drive. The hinge joint is the workhorse of mechanical constraint — one rotational degree of freedom, producing everything from doors to engines. Here it lifts a bridge, making the constraint visible as architecture.
DrawbridgeHinge.name: DrawbridgeHinge
DrawbridgeHinge.qfep_connection: Pure F — the hinge joint as the most intuitive constraint: one axis of rotation, everything else locked. The motor adds controllable energy, turning the constraint into a machine.
DrawbridgeHinge.gamwell_reference: Hinge mechanics, motorized joints, drawbridge engineering, single-axis rotation, torque and angular velocity
interactions: press up/down arrow keys to control bridge motor velocity
watch idle oscillation when no keys are pressed
observe the hinge limit preventing over-rotation
DrawbridgeHinge.capacity: CONTROL a motorized hinge joint and explain how angular limits and motor velocity combine to create mechanical behavior.

GimbalStabilizer.description: A dual-hinge gimbal system with independent yaw and pitch control. Two motor-driven hinges are stacked orthogonally: one rotates freely around the vertical axis (yaw), the other is limited to plus-or-minus 45 degrees on the horizontal axis (pitch). Together they aim a payload in 3D space. The idle mode sweeps smoothly through a Lissajous-like pattern; arrow keys override with direct motor control. This demonstrates how composing multiple single-axis joints creates multi-axis articulation.
GimbalStabilizer.name: GimbalStabilizer
GimbalStabilizer.qfep_connection: Composed F — two hinge constraints stacked orthogonally, each removing one degree of freedom while their composition allows two-axis aiming. The gimbal is Form squared: constraint upon constraint yielding expressive control.
GimbalStabilizer.gamwell_reference: Gimbal systems, multi-axis rotation, Euler angles and gimbal lock, camera stabilization, robotic actuators, Lissajous figures
interactions: press arrow keys to override yaw and pitch motors
watch the idle Lissajous-like sweep pattern
observe how pitch limits constrain vertical range while yaw is free
GimbalStabilizer.capacity: COMPOSE two orthogonal hinge joints into a gimbal system and predict how independent motor control on each axis produces 2D aiming.

HingeCrank.description: A motorized crank mechanism combining three joint types into one machine. A hinge joint spins a wheel at constant velocity, a pin joint connects the wheel to a sliding rod, and a slider joint guides the rod along a rail. The result is rotary-to-linear conversion — the fundamental mechanism behind pistons, steam engines, and sewing machines. Watch how continuous rotation becomes reciprocating translation through the geometry of constraint.
HingeCrank.name: HingeCrank
HingeCrank.qfep_connection: Classical F — three constraint rules (hinge, pin, slider) composed into a mechanism. Each joint removes degrees of freedom; together they channel rotary energy into linear work.
HingeCrank.gamwell_reference: Crank-slider mechanism, rotary-to-linear conversion, Watt linkage, mechanical advantage, kinematics of machines
interactions: watch the motor-driven wheel spin and push the rod
observe how rotation converts to linear reciprocation
notice the slider rail constraining the rod's path
HingeCrank.capacity: DESCRIBE how combining hinge, pin, and slider joints converts rotary motion to linear motion in a crank-slider mechanism.

IKArm.description: FABRIK inverse kinematics on a 4-segment arm — target orbits, arm solves backward and forward

PendulumPin.description: The simplest joint demo — a single sphere suspended from a fixed anchor by a pin joint. Gravity pulls the bob down; the pin constraint keeps it tethered, converting potential energy into angular motion. The bob swings freely in 3D, slowly decaying as linear damping bleeds energy. This is the atom of the joints sequence: one constraint, one body, one degree of freedom worth watching.
PendulumPin.name: PendulumPin
PendulumPin.qfep_connection: Pure F — a single constraint rule (the pin) producing predictable periodic motion. The pendulum is Form at its most elementary: structure yields behavior.
PendulumPin.gamwell_reference: Simple pendulum mechanics, Galileo's isochronism, harmonic motion, single degree-of-freedom systems
interactions: watch the bob swing from its initial nudge
press space to apply an impulse and restart the swing
observe how damping gradually reduces the arc
PendulumPin.capacity: EXPLAIN how a pin joint constrains motion to rotation around a fixed point and how damping converts oscillation into stillness.

SliderPress.description: A piston and rail system demonstrating the slider joint — one translational degree of freedom. The piston oscillates along a Z-axis track with controllable motor speed and force via VR sliders. Real-time labels show position and velocity, making the relationship between motor parameters and motion directly readable. The slider joint is the opposite of a hinge: where hinges permit rotation and forbid translation, sliders permit translation and forbid rotation.
SliderPress.name: SliderPress
SliderPress.qfep_connection: Classical F — the slider joint as a constraint that channels energy into exactly one translational axis. Motor speed and force become controllable parameters that the learner tunes to feel the difference between velocity and impulse.
SliderPress.gamwell_reference: Linear actuators, prismatic joints, piston mechanics, controllable force systems, degrees of freedom in mechanisms
interactions: adjust the speed slider to control oscillation frequency
adjust the force slider to control piston push strength
read position and velocity labels in real time
compare slider behavior with hinge rotation
SliderPress.capacity: TUNE motor speed and force parameters to control a slider joint's translational motion and read the resulting position and velocity.

SpringSuspension.description: A car-like suspension system using a Generic6DOF joint configured as a vertical spring. A wheel hangs below a chassis, free to bounce vertically but locked in all other axes. The spring stiffness and damping create the characteristic suspension feel — press space to drop the wheel and watch it oscillate to rest. This demonstrates how a single 6DOF joint with carefully chosen axis locks and spring parameters can simulate complex mechanical behavior.
SpringSuspension.name: SpringSuspension
SpringSuspension.qfep_connection: Classical F with lambda-tuning — the 6DOF joint's spring stiffness and damping are the lambda parameters that tune between rigid constraint (high stiffness) and free motion (low stiffness). The sweet spot produces naturalistic suspension.
SpringSuspension.gamwell_reference: Spring-damper systems, suspension mechanics, Generic6DOF joints, Hooke's law in constrained systems, shock absorber dynamics
interactions: press space to bounce the wheel and watch it oscillate
notice how vertical motion is free but lateral motion is locked
SpringSuspension.capacity: EXPLAIN how a 6DOF joint with spring parameters on one axis and locks on all others creates suspension behavior.

algo_gun.description: Evolved gravity gun that captures and directs Grid Agents. Use GRIP button to capture agents, then aim and GRIP again to direct them to modify grid structures.
algo_gun.name: Algo-Gun

bouncing_ball.capacity: SEE that the bounce coefficient controls how much chaos (energy) survives each collision
bouncing_ball.description: The quintessential physics demo: a ball bouncing under gravity with configurable coefficient of restitution. At e=1.0, perfectly elastic — energy conserved, bounces forever. Below 1.0, each impact dissipates energy as heat and sound, and the ball gradually dies. A complete parabolic trajectory with collision response in the simplest possible package.
bouncing_ball.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
bouncing_ball.name: Bouncing Ball
bouncing_ball.qfep_connection: Pure F — gravity pulls, floor reflects. The simplest possible physics: one force, one constraint. The bounce coefficient IS lambda: 1.0 = perfect (no energy loss), 0.0 = dead stop.

cloth_simulation.description: A grid of particles connected by structural, shear, and bend springs forming a deformable cloth surface. Responds to gravity, wind forces, and collisions. Pin corners and watch it drape; release and watch it fall. The interplay of thousands of tiny spring forces creating fluid, fabric-like motion from purely mechanical rules.
cloth_simulation.name: Cloth Simulation
cloth_simulation.qfep_connection: Cloth as emergent softness — rigid spring rules at the micro level produce flowing, organic behavior at the macro level. The visual gap between the grid topology and the draped result is emergence made visible.

collision_detection.description: Two-phase collision detection pipeline: broad phase (spatial hashing, bounding boxes) rapidly culls impossible pairs, then narrow phase (GJK/SAT algorithms) computes exact contact points, penetration depth, and collision normals. Visualizes the acceleration structures that make real-time physics possible — without them, checking every pair is O(n²) death.
collision_detection.name: Collision Detection
collision_detection.qfep_connection: Collision detection as the boundary between order and disorder — the moment two objects meet is a phase transition where kinetic energy redistributes. The algorithm itself is a lambda that converts spatial proximity into contact events.

constraints.capacity: SEE that each constraint removes a degree of freedom — freedom is defined by what is forbidden
constraints.description: Joint constraints that restrict rigid body degrees of freedom: hinges (1 rotational DOF), sliders (1 translational DOF), ball-and-socket (3 rotational DOF), and fixed joints. Watch how iterative constraint solvers project invalid states back onto the constraint manifold, enforcing physical laws as geometric relationships.
constraints.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
interactions: compare hinge vs slider vs ball
constraints.name: Constraints & Joints
constraints.qfep_connection: F-limitation — joints restrict degrees of freedom. Each constraint removes a possibility. A hinge allows rotation but forbids translation. Freedom is defined by what is forbidden.

example_1_10_accelerating_towards_the_mo.name: example_1_10_accelerating_towards_the_mouse_vr
example_1_10_accelerating_towards_the_mo.qfep_connection: The mouse is gone; in VR the mover chases an autonomous target riding its own sine orbits, acceleration always aimed at where the target is, never where it will be. Desire as steering deficit — constant pursuit, perpetual lag, the status label narrating the gap.

example_2_1_forces_vr.description: Force application demo — applying a force vector to a body and watching F=ma unfold. Nature of Code chapter 2.1.
example_2_1_forces_vr.name: Forces (2.1)

example_2_5_fluid_resistance_vr.capacity: FEEL that drag is the medium's memory of your velocity — the faster you move, the harder the world pushes back
example_2_5_fluid_resistance_vr.description: Drag opposes motion and scales with speed squared. Heavier objects fall faster through the same fluid. F_drag = -C * |v|^2 * v-hat. The faster you move, the harder the world pushes back.
example_2_5_fluid_resistance_vr.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
example_2_5_fluid_resistance_vr.name: example_2_5_fluid_resistance_vr
example_2_5_fluid_resistance_vr.qfep_connection: F-resistance — drag is the medium's memory of your velocity. A feedback loop: speed creates resistance, resistance limits speed. Equilibrium is negotiation.

example_3_10_swinging_pendulum_vr.name: example_3_10_swinging_pendulum_vr
example_3_10_swinging_pendulum_vr.qfep_connection: Gravity is a slider and arm length another, so the pendulum's period stops being a fact of the world and becomes a negotiation at the rack. What no knob touches is the form itself — acceleration drawn from the sine of the angle — the law outlives every parameter you betray.

example_3_11_a_spring_connection_vr.name: example_3_11_a_spring_connection_vr
example_3_11_a_spring_connection_vr.qfep_connection: Hooke's law is punishment proportional to distance from a rest length the spring believes in. With K, DAMP, and REST all on sliders, the norm itself becomes adjustable — you can move the ideal anywhere, but the bob is still corrected toward wherever it currently sits.

example_3_1_angular_motion_using_rotate_.name: example_3_1_angular_motion_using_rotate_vr
example_3_1_angular_motion_using_rotate_.qfep_connection: Rotation taught as bookkeeping: one accumulator incremented every frame, a degree readout confessing that the beam never knows its angle, only how much has been added. Sign the slider negative and time runs backward for free — the physics was never more than arithmetic with a direction.

example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angula.capacity: SEE that rotation and translation are independent stories told by the same body
example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angula.description: Eight boxes orbit an attractor while spinning at their own rate — rotation and translation coexisting as independent freedoms. Linear attraction pulls them inward while random angular impulses accumulate, making each box spin differently. Movers wrap at boundaries creating toroidal space. Rotation does not need a force — it needs a torque, or random impulses.
example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angula.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, Nature of Code
interactions: adjust attractor strength via VR slider
example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angula.name: Arbitrary Angular Motion
example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angula.qfep_connection: Two independent F channels — linear attraction is one deterministic force, angular impulses are another. Lambda is the angular damping: high damping kills spin (pure orbital F), low damping lets chaos into rotation while translation stays ordered.

example_3_3_pointing_in_the_direction_of.capacity: FEEL that heading is not chosen but inherited from motion — direction of motion IS orientation
example_3_3_pointing_in_the_direction_of.description: A cone that always points where it is going — orientation derived from velocity, not set independently. Sinusoidal thrust drives the mover in Lissajous-like 3D curves. The cone's nose traces the velocity vector, making heading a consequence of movement. A thing that points where it moves has surrendered its identity to its velocity.
example_3_3_pointing_in_the_direction_of.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, Nature of Code
interactions: adjust thrust magnitude via VR slider
see orientation lag during direction changes
example_3_3_pointing_in_the_direction_of.name: Pointing in Direction of Motion
example_3_3_pointing_in_the_direction_of.qfep_connection: F-alignment — the cone's orientation IS its velocity direction. No independent rotation. Identity (heading) is fully determined by dynamics (velocity). Pure F: given the state, the orientation is computable.

example_3_4_polar_to_cartesian_vr.description: Polar to cartesian coordinate conversion demonstration
example_3_4_polar_to_cartesian_vr.name: example_3_4_polar_to_cartesian_vr
example_3_4_polar_to_cartesian_vr.qfep_connection: One number accumulates — angle plus speed, every frame — and the conversion turns that single degree of freedom into a circle's worth of positions. The trail makes the translation visible: what reads as motion through space is bookkeeping in a friendlier coordinate system.

example_3_5_simple_harmonic_motion_vr.description: Damped harmonic motion with coupled oscillators, beats/resonance detection, energy bars (KE/PE/total), decay envelope, and VR slider controls
example_3_5_simple_harmonic_motion_vr.name: example_3_5_simple_harmonic_motion_vr
example_3_5_simple_harmonic_motion_vr.qfep_connection: Two bobs, one damped, one coupled, their kinetic and potential energy drawn as live bars while damping quietly bleeds the total: E_flux made ledger-visible. The beats that appear belong to neither oscillator — the pattern lives in the coupling, an emergence you can watch being paid for.

example_3_6_simple_harmonic_motion_ii_vr.description: Simple harmonic motion part II demonstration
example_3_6_simple_harmonic_motion_ii_vr.name: example_3_6_simple_harmonic_motion_ii_vr
example_3_6_simple_harmonic_motion_ii_vr.qfep_connection: One sine on x, another on y, and the bob's trail draws a figure neither frequency contains. The Lissajous curve is a relation made flesh: touch either amplitude slider and the trail is wiped, because the drawing belongs to the ratio, not to the parts.

example_3_7_oscillator_objects_vr.name: example_3_7_oscillator_objects_vr
example_3_7_oscillator_objects_vr.qfep_connection: Ten rods share one class and one clock; randf hands each its private amplitude, period, and phase. Individuality here is exactly the seed — same code, different draw — and the single Global Speed slider quietly proves the whole diverse population runs on one throttle.

example_3_8_static_wave_vr.description: Wave superposition with two traveling waves, constructive/destructive interference coloring, and 2D wave equation membrane (finite difference PDE with boundary reflection)
example_3_8_static_wave_vr.name: example_3_8_static_wave_vr
example_3_8_static_wave_vr.qfep_connection: Superposition color-coded as verdict: green where two waves agree, red where they annihilate, and behind them a finite-difference membrane where each cell consults only its neighbors. Interference is what the sum knows that neither wave does — knowledge that exists nowhere but in the adding.

example_3_9_the_wave_vr.name: example_3_9_the_wave_vr
example_3_9_the_wave_vr.qfep_connection: Every point only bobs in place; what travels is phase. Theta advances, the mesh stays put, and the eye insists on a moving thing anyway — the wave is an object the player believes in that the code never constructed.

example_6_1_basic_rigidbody_vr.name: Basic Rigidbody VR
example_6_1_basic_rigidbody_vr.qfep_connection: One pink box, one grey plane, and a fall that is written nowhere in the script: the code declares mass and shape, then cedes motion to a solver it never sees. The chapter's first lesson is delegated causality — from here on, behavior is something you configure a stranger to produce.

example_6_2_falling_boxes_vr.name: Falling Boxes VR
example_6_2_falling_boxes_vr.qfep_connection: A box of random size and mass every half second, capped at thirty, silently deleted below y = −1: abundance staged with a janitor. The pile reads as endless flux only because removal is quieter than arrival — E_flux on a memory budget, entropy with a cleanup crew.

example_6_3_compound_bodies_vr.name: Compound Bodies VR
example_6_3_compound_bodies_vr.qfep_connection: Dumbbell, T, L, cross — several collision shapes, one rigid body, one shared velocity. Compoundness stages identity as a solver-level fiction: the parts don't cohere materially, they have signed a constraint agreeing to move as one, and rigidity is the name of that treaty holding.

example_6_4_windmill_vr.name: Windmill VR
example_6_4_windmill_vr.qfep_connection: The wind is a motor parameter on a hinge joint, and everything else — velocity-colored blades, torque arrows, synthesized whoosh keyed to RPM — labors to make that parameter feel like weather. Instrumentation as persuasion: the more sensors the scene grows, the better it hides that the atmosphere is an actuator setting.

example_6_5_chain_vr.name: Chain VR
example_6_5_chain_vr.qfep_connection: Eight rigid links, each bound to the last by a Generic6DOFJoint: rope as the limit of hinged stiffness, flexibility existing nowhere except between the parts. Grabbing the end and grabbing the middle redistribute constraint differently down the line — where you hold the chain decides what the rest of it is free to do.

example_6_6_grab_vr.name: Grab VR
example_6_6_grab_vr.qfep_connection: Grabbing is implemented as a six-degree-of-freedom joint snapped between hand and body: physics has no concept of holding, only constraint, so possession is staged as a temporary contract the solver keeps honoring.

example_6_7_bridge_vr.name: Bridge VR
example_6_7_bridge_vr.qfep_connection: Held at both ends and hinged everywhere between, the deck's sag is never drawn — it is the twelve joints' running settlement with each ball the two-second timer drops. Load-testing as ambient ritual: the span stays believable only while something keeps falling on it.

example_6_8_collision_layers_vr.name: Collision Layers VR
example_6_8_collision_layers_vr.qfep_connection: Pink touches pink, blue touches blue, green touches only the ground — bodies sharing one space while bitmasks decide who is real to whom. Segregation implemented as physics: invisible, wholly consequential, and printed on a legend no body inside the simulation can read.

exercise_3_11_oop_wave_vr.name: exercise_3_11_oop_wave_vr
exercise_3_11_oop_wave_vr.qfep_connection: The wave becomes an object: amplitude, wavelength, speed as fields, update() as its entire life. The sliders speak to the class and never to the mesh — motion administered through an interface, which is encapsulation's real promise and its real distance.

exercise_3_12_additive_wave_vr.name: exercise_3_12_additive_wave_vr
exercise_3_12_additive_wave_vr.qfep_connection: Up to eight random sines summed into one line, and dragging the WAVES slider re-rolls the entire ensemble rather than extending it. The sum is cheap to make and impossible to invert — no bump on the curve will ever confess which component put it there.

exercise_3_15_double_pendulum_vr.name: exercise_3_15_double_pendulum_vr
exercise_3_15_double_pendulum_vr.qfep_connection: Two arms and one gravity constant are enough to break prediction: the second bob drags a trail that is sensitivity to initial angles made watchable at arm's length, entropy drawn in the air.

exercise_3_1_baton_vr.name: exercise_3_1_baton_vr
exercise_3_1_baton_vr.qfep_connection: One angular velocity for the whole rigid bar, but only the weighted ends pay for it in distance, their trails ringing the pivot in circles the bar itself never draws. Rotation is shared equally and experienced unequally — position in the body decides the cost.

exercise_3_5_spiral_vr.name: exercise_3_5_spiral_vr
exercise_3_5_spiral_vr.qfep_connection: Two rules — angle grows, radius grows with it — accumulate a polar line into a spiral. Move the Growth slider and every point is erased back to zero: the form can absorb new speed mid-flight, but a new law demands the whole history be redrawn.

exercise_3_6_asteroids_vr.name: exercise_3_6_asteroids_vr
exercise_3_6_asteroids_vr.qfep_connection: Thrust, turn, drift, wraparound — the full grammar of piloting — but the pilot is sin(t) and cos(t) on the system clock. Agency staged with no agent in it: the controls were translated into weather, and the ship performs being flown forever.

fem_simulation.description: Finite Element Method (FEM) for deformable solid mechanics. A continuous body is discretized into tetrahedral or hexahedral elements, each computing stress and strain from local deformation gradients. Assemble the global stiffness matrix, solve the linear system, and watch beams bend, bridges sag, and materials yield under load — engineering simulation made visible.
fem_simulation.name: Finite Element Method
fem_simulation.qfep_connection: FEM as discretized order — the continuous stress field (infinite-dimensional) projected onto a finite basis of shape functions. Each element is a local lambda mapping displacement to force; the assembled system is emergent global behavior from local constitutive laws.

firework_launcher.capacity: SEE that a firework is a population explosion — one event becomes many independent paths, each obeying the same law
firework_launcher.description: Launch rockets that climb, then explode into showers of glowing particles — each one a tiny body under gravity, drag, and fading lifetime. Four color presets (classic, ocean, garden, ring pattern) create distinct particle distributions. Shows particle emission, statistical spread, force application to many bodies, and emergent visual patterns from simple rules.
firework_launcher.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
interactions: observe drag and gravity on each particle
firework_launcher.name: Firework Launcher
firework_launcher.qfep_connection: phi-dE — one launch event becomes sixty independent trajectories. The explosion is a burst of dE, each particle's drag coefficient is phi damping the change. One cause, many effects.

fluid_simulation.description: Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) fluid simulation — the Navier-Stokes equations approximated by a cloud of particles carrying mass, velocity, and pressure. Kernel functions smooth physical quantities over neighbor particles, producing viscous flow, surface tension, and splashing. The Lagrangian approach to fluid dynamics where the fluid carries its own computational grid.
fluid_simulation.name: Fluid Simulation (SPH)
fluid_simulation.qfep_connection: Fluid as the continuum limit of particle interactions — pressure enforces incompressibility (order), viscosity dissipates vortices (entropy), and turbulence is the perpetual negotiation between them. SPH kernels are the lambda functions that interpolate local physics.

force_fields.capacity: FEEL that a force field is a region with different rules — cross the boundary and the laws change
force_fields.description: Configurable force fields — uniform gravity, directional wind, radial attraction/repulsion, and vortex fields — applied to populations of particles. Combine multiple fields to create complex flow patterns. Each field type is a spatial function mapping position to force: F(x) defines the landscape that particles navigate.
force_fields.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
interactions: observe balls entering different force zones
watch directional push vs radial pull vs viscous drag
force_fields.name: Force Fields
force_fields.qfep_connection: Regional F — three zones with three different force laws. Cross a boundary and physics changes. Lambda is spatial: the same object experiences different forces depending on where it is.

friction_ramp.capacity: FEEL how friction coefficient controls the balance between motion and resistance on an inclined plane
friction_ramp.description: Inclined plane with adjustable friction coefficient and slope angle. A block slides or sticks based on whether mg·sin(θ) exceeds μ·mg·cos(θ). Force arrows show gravity, normal force, and friction in real time. VR sliders control μ (0–1.5) and angle (5°–60°).
friction_ramp.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
friction_ramp.name: Friction Ramp
friction_ramp.qfep_connection: F-resistance on a surface — friction converts kinetic energy to heat. The coefficient of friction is lambda: zero means frictionless (pure F), high means the surface dominates.

gravity_well.capacity: FEEL that gravity is not a force but a curvature — objects follow the shape of warped space
gravity_well.description: The rubber-sheet metaphor made real: a deformable grid mesh warps around a movable mass, creating a visible gravitational well. Colored test particles roll along the curved surface, orbiting, spiraling inward, or escaping depending on their velocity. Adjustable mass strength deepens or flattens the well in real time.
gravity_well.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
gravity_well.name: Gravity Well
gravity_well.qfep_connection: F as geometry — the rubber sheet metaphor. Mass warps space, and objects follow the curvature. Force is not a push — it is the shape of the world.

lifetime_curves.description: Three emitters demonstrating color, size, and opacity curves over particle lifetime

magnetic_simulation.description: Magnetic field simulation with dipoles, field line visualization, and Lorentz force on charged particles. Watch iron filings align along field lines, see how bar magnets attract and repel, and observe charged particles spiraling in helical paths through uniform fields. Maxwell's equations made tangible through interactive electromagnetic landscapes.
magnetic_simulation.name: Magnetic Field Simulation
magnetic_simulation.qfep_connection: Magnetism as invisible order — field lines are the hidden structure that organizes matter at a distance. The Lorentz force is the lambda coupling charge velocity to magnetic field, producing the perpendicular deflection that makes electric motors and particle accelerators possible.

mass_spring_damper.capacity: UNDERSTAND that every vibrating system is a mass-spring-damper in disguise — the damping ratio is the system's temperament
mass_spring_damper.description: The canonical second-order system: a mass on a spring with viscous damping. Hooke's law (F = -kx) provides the restoring force, damping (F = -cv) dissipates energy. Explore underdamped oscillation, critical damping, and overdamped decay by tweaking spring stiffness k and damping coefficient c. The foundation of every vibration analysis ever performed.
mass_spring_damper.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
mass_spring_damper.name: Mass-Spring-Damper
mass_spring_damper.qfep_connection: Classical F with damping — the spring IS F (restoring order), the damper IS lambda (how fast chaos dissipates). Three regimes at three damping ratios: underdamped, critical, overdamped.

momentum_collision.name: Momentum Collision
momentum_collision.description: Physical momentum and collision demonstration. Objects collide with realistic mass transfer — shows conservation of momentum and the invisible forces governing motion.
momentum_collision.qfep_connection: Force (F) as momentum transfer — the measurable push that changes system state.

nbody_simulation.capacity: WATCH emergent orbital structure arise from nothing but pairwise gravity
nbody_simulation.description: N-body gravitational simulation where every mass attracts every other mass via Newton's law of gravitation (F = Gm₁m₂/r²). Watch galaxies form, binary stars orbit, and clusters scatter. The O(n²) pairwise force computation is the computational bottleneck that drove the invention of Barnes-Hut trees and fast multipole methods.
nbody_simulation.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
nbody_simulation.name: N-Body Gravitational Simulation
nbody_simulation.qfep_connection: N-body F scaling — as N grows, pairwise interactions create emergent structure (orbits, clusters, ejections) that no single force law predicts. Complexity from simple rules.

newton_cradle.capacity: SEE that momentum transfers through a chain — the middle balls are messengers, not movers
newton_cradle.description: The iconic desktop physics demo: 5 pendulum balls suspended from a frame. Pull one back and release — momentum transfers through elastic collisions, ball-by-ball. Shows conservation of momentum and energy, elastic collision mechanics, and the satisfying click-clack of F=ma made tangible.
newton_cradle.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
newton_cradle.name: Newton's Cradle
newton_cradle.qfep_connection: F-conservation — momentum and energy transfer through a chain of collisions. What enters on one side exits on the other. The middle balls appear still but carry the signal.

newtons_laws.description: Interactive visualization of Newton's three laws of motion: inertia (an object at rest stays at rest), F=ma (force produces acceleration proportional to mass), and action-reaction (every force has an equal opposite). Objects of varying mass respond to applied forces, making the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration viscerally tangible.
newtons_laws.name: Newton's Laws
newtons_laws.qfep_connection: Newton's laws as the foundational grammar of physical order — F=ma is the simplest lambda mapping force to motion, the irreducible rule from which all mechanical complexity emerges.

numerical_integration.description: Side-by-side comparison of numerical integration schemes: forward Euler (simple but drifty), symplectic Euler (energy-preserving), and RK4 (fourth-order accuracy). Watch identical initial conditions diverge as each method accumulates different error profiles over time. The gap between the curves is the price of computational shortcuts.
numerical_integration.name: Numerical Integration Methods
numerical_integration.qfep_connection: Integration methods as different lambda functions approximating the same continuous truth — discretization introduces entropy (numerical error), and the choice of method determines how much order is preserved across time steps.

particle_campfire.description: Synthesis campfire combining fire, embers, and smoke particle systems

particle_systems.capacity: SEE how thousands of deterministic particles produce statistical, entropic behavior
particle_systems.description: Particle emitters spawning thousands of particles with configurable lifetimes, initial velocities, forces, and visual properties. Particles are born, live under physics, and die — creating fire, smoke, sparks, and rain from simple statistical rules. Each particle is independent, yet the ensemble produces coherent visual phenomena.
particle_systems.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
particle_systems.name: Particle Systems
particle_systems.qfep_connection: E(S) from F — each particle obeys deterministic forces, but thousands of them produce statistical behavior. Individual determinism creates collective entropy.

raycastingpoints.description: Interactive raycasting algorithm visualization with point-based collision detection
raycastingpoints.name: Raycasting Points
raycastingpoints.qfep_connection: Three thousand particles obey eight attractors that exist only as shader uniforms; the rays are never drawn, just their consequences. Force made visible exclusively through the bodies it disturbs — you reconstruct the beam from the behaviour of the crowd.

rigid_body.description: Full rigid body simulation with linear and angular motion. Watch objects translate, rotate, and tumble under applied forces and torques. Demonstrates moment of inertia tensors, angular momentum conservation, and the coupling between linear and rotational dynamics that makes a thrown wrench wobble differently than a thrown ball.
rigid_body.name: Rigid Body Dynamics
rigid_body.qfep_connection: Rigid bodies as the emergence of rotational complexity from simple force rules — angular momentum conservation as a deep symmetry (Noether's theorem), where rotational order persists even as translational chaos increases.

simulation_instability.description: Spring system with ramping timestep — watch stable oscillation drift, then explode as dt grows too large

slingshot_launcher.description: Step onto the platform and get catapulted! A charging catapult mechanism detects the player, builds power, then fires you (and demo balls) along a parabolic trajectory. Adjustable launch angle and power with a visible trajectory preview. Shows impulse, projectile motion, and the visceral thrill of Newton's third law.
slingshot_launcher.name: Slingshot Launcher
slingshot_launcher.qfep_connection: Impulse — a short burst of force that changes everything. The launcher is a delta function: infinite force for zero time, producing finite momentum.

soft_bodies.description: Soft body deformation using pressure-volume models and shape matching. Objects squish, stretch, and jiggle while maintaining approximate volume — like jelly, rubber, or biological tissue. Combines ideas from spring networks, FEM, and position-based dynamics into satisfying, tactile deformation that you want to poke.
soft_bodies.name: Soft Body Physics
soft_bodies.qfep_connection: Soft bodies as elastic memory — deformed states always remember and seek their rest shape (order), while external forces and collisions continuously perturb them (entropy). The wobble is the visible oscillation between imposed disorder and intrinsic structure.

softmill.name: softmill
softmill.qfep_connection: oscillation: a soft mill — compliant blades behind frosted glass, turned by the same physics they yield to. Where a rigid mill imposes its cycle, this one negotiates every revolution with the bodies it meets; the machine itself is soft, so work and deformation are the same event.

spring_mass_system.description: A network of point masses connected by springs, forming a deformable mesh. Energy propagates as waves through the lattice — pluck one node and watch the disturbance ripple outward. The discrete analog of a continuous elastic medium, and the building block for cloth, soft bodies, and lattice dynamics.
spring_mass_system.name: Spring-Mass Network
spring_mass_system.qfep_connection: Emergence of wave behavior from purely local spring interactions — no node knows about the global pattern, yet coherent waves arise. Individual springs are simple lambdas; their network produces emergent order.

spring_system.capacity: SEE that a spring network is a medium — perturbation at one point travels through connections
spring_system.description: System-level spring behavior exploring coupled oscillators, resonance, and energy transfer between connected springs. When natural frequencies align, energy sloshes back and forth between modes in beautiful beat patterns. Demonstrates normal modes and the spectral decomposition of complex vibrations into simple harmonic components.
spring_system.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
interactions: perturb one mass and watch wave propagate
spring_system.name: Spring System
spring_system.qfep_connection: F as network — each spring enforces Hooke's law locally, but the network produces wave propagation globally. Structure creates communication.

sub_emitters.description: Firework mortar launching projectiles that spawn burst particles on death

surreal_kinetic_sculpture.description: An art installation that weaves together multiple physics systems — springs, rigid bodies, constraints, particles, and forces — into a mesmerizing, perpetually-moving kinetic sculpture. Gears drive pendulums that scatter particles through force fields while cloth banners ripple in simulated wind. Not a tutorial but a celebration: physics as aesthetic experience, computation as art.
surreal_kinetic_sculpture.name: Surreal Kinetic Sculpture
surreal_kinetic_sculpture.qfep_connection: The sculpture as physics made beautiful — all the individual simulation techniques unified into a single emergent artwork. Each subsystem contributes its lambda; the whole is irreducible to its parts. The QFEP synthesis: order (structure), entropy (motion), lambda (physics rules), emergence (art).

three_body_problem.capacity: WITNESS that three bodies under gravity have no formula — determinism and predictability are not the same thing
three_body_problem.description: The infamous three-body problem: three gravitationally interacting masses with no closed-form solution. Tiny changes in initial conditions lead to wildly divergent trajectories — the original exemplar of deterministic chaos. Explore stable figure-eight orbits, Lagrange points, and the chaotic regime where prediction becomes impossible.
three_body_problem.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
three_body_problem.name: Three-Body Problem
three_body_problem.qfep_connection: Deterministic chaos — pure F (gravity), no randomness, yet unpredictable. Lambda emerges from sensitivity to initial conditions. Three bodies prove that determinism and predictability are not the same.

tscn_joint.description: A static reference scene showing multiple joint types side by side for comparison. Demonstrates the visual difference between pin, hinge, slider, cone-twist, and 6DOF joints in a single exhibit. Used as an overview or index artifact at the start of the joints sequence.
tscn_joint.name: tscn_joint
tscn_joint.qfep_connection: Pure F — a taxonomy of constraints. Each joint type removes different degrees of freedom; seeing them together reveals the design space of mechanical connection.
tscn_joint.gamwell_reference: Joint taxonomy, degrees of freedom comparison, constraint classification, mechanical connection types
interactions: walk between joint exhibits to compare constraint types
observe which axes each joint type permits or restricts
tscn_joint.capacity: CLASSIFY joint types by the degrees of freedom they permit and predict which joint is appropriate for a given mechanical task.

vector_fields.capacity: SEE the force before the object arrives — the field exists everywhere, waiting
vector_fields.description: 3D vector field visualization with arrow glyphs showing direction and magnitude at grid points. Particles advected through the field trace streamlines, revealing the flow structure — sources, sinks, saddle points, and vortices. Includes curl, divergence, and gradient field types with real-time parameter control.
vector_fields.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
interactions: watch field lines and flow patterns
vector_fields.name: Vector Fields
vector_fields.qfep_connection: F made visible — every point in space has an arrow. The field IS the force before any object arrives to feel it. Potential becomes actual only at the point of contact.

verlet_integration.capacity: UNDERSTAND that the most stable integration method forgot to track velocity — positions remember
verlet_integration.description: Position-based Verlet integration — the workhorse of game physics and molecular dynamics. Instead of tracking velocity explicitly, it infers motion from the difference between current and previous positions. This makes it naturally stable, time-reversible, and beautifully simple: x_new = 2x_current - x_old + a·dt².
verlet_integration.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
verlet_integration.name: Verlet Integration
verlet_integration.qfep_connection: F-computation — the most stable integration method works by forgetting velocity. Position history encodes all the information. Simpler representation, better stability.

viscosity_layers.description: Three transparent columns side by side — air, water, and honey. Drop identical balls into all three simultaneously and watch them descend at wildly different rates. Quadratic drag makes the honey ball crawl while the air ball plummets. Real-time speed readouts let you compare terminal velocities directly.
viscosity_layers.name: Viscosity Layers
viscosity_layers.qfep_connection: Resistance as information — the medium tells you what it's made of. Drag is the environment's signature, entropy in the friction between motion and medium.

waterflowers.description: Artistic water simulation with flower-like patterns and organic fluid behavior
waterflowers.name: Water Flowers
waterflowers.qfep_connection: The surface is four Gerstner waves computed twice — once in the shader for the eye, once on the CPU so fifty rigid-body flowers can spring toward the same height. Floating is the moment the water's two representations agree.

waterone.description: Advanced water simulation algorithm with realistic fluid dynamics and surface tension
waterone.name: Water One
waterone.qfep_connection: The reflection is a second camera hung upside-down beneath the plane, re-rendering the world at 512 squared every frame; the waves are three sine terms summed in a vertex shader. Nothing here is fluid — 'water' is the name granted to any surface that performs mirroring and undulation convincingly enough.

registry_info.description: Physics simulation artifacts — from Newton's laws and numerical integration through rigid bodies, spring systems, fluid dynamics, and beyond. A comprehensive tour of classical mechanics rendered interactive.
registry_info.name: physics_simulation
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods (Euler/Verlet/RK4), continuum mechanics, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian frameworks, computational physics
